A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same BiMark research work. All 20 pages of each version, including the figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermark extraction, detection, downstream-task, and ablation results in Section 5, plus paraphrasing-attack results in Appendix B and generated-text examples in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendices B and D, including Tables 2–5 and Figures 4–5.

M1.justification: The bit-flip reweighting, multilayer composition, XOR-based message encoding, and voting-based extraction procedures are unchanged. Appendix C retains identical algorithms; revisions to Figure 1 concern its illustrative example.

E1.justification: Both versions use C4-RealNewslike prompts, CNN/DailyMail summarization, and WMT’16 English–Romanian translation. Zero-bit and multi-bit watermarking, synonym substitution, and Appendix B’s DIPPER paraphrasing scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: MPAC in Tables 2–3; Soft Red List and SynthID in Figure 4; the same unwatermarked and watermarking baselines in Table 4; and Soft Red List, SynthID, and DiPmark in Table 5. Updated citation years do not introduce different baselines.

E3.justification: The reported models, metrics, message and text lengths, attack settings, and generation parameters are unchanged. Both versions specify temperature 1.0, top-50 sampling, a two-token context window, and the same BiMark and baseline configurations.

E4.justification: Both retain the computational-cost analysis, four multilayer ablation analyses in Section 5.3, synonym-substitution tests, Appendix B’s paraphrasing tests, and Appendix D’s examples. No analysis question or supporting evidence is added or removed.

E5.justification: Table 4 retains the same plus/minus reporting, and Figures 4–5 retain their shaded bands. There are no added or revised repeated-run counts, seed disclosures, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Experimental values and findings in Tables 2–5, Figures 4–5, and Appendix D are unchanged. For example, Table 2 reports BiMark’s 95.26% extraction rate and 8.5 perplexity for eight-bit messages in 50-token texts in both versions. Figure 1’s revised vote annotations are schematic rather than experimental results.

T1.justification: The definitions, scaling-factor derivation, unbiasedness theorem, and Appendix A proofs retain the same mathematical substance. Changing E to e in Definition 3.2 and Pr to P in Appendix A standardizes notation without revising assumptions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three contributions and claims about quality preservation, model-agnostic detection, and message capacity, including up to 30% higher extraction rates for short texts.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning stronger shallow-layer contributions, deterioration with excessive layers, and resilience from multiple watermark signals are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same high-entropy applicability discussion; no substantive limitation or qualification is added.

D1.justification: The code-access statement, generation settings, watermark hyperparameters, pseudocode, and reported token-generation timings are unchanged. Updated references provide bibliographic information rather than new implementation or reproducibility instructions.

R1.justification: The introduction replaces Guan et al. (2023), a traffic-prediction reference, with Feng and Dai (2023), a link-prediction reference. Most other reference edits update existing works to publication versions or consolidate duplicate entries; the substantive watermarking research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 updates citation years and publication metadata, standardizes mathematical notation, and makes limited diagram-label edits. The section organization, appendix structure, and substantive prose are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 3 receive limited graphical and typesetting revisions. Figure 1 changes the example index from p = 3 to p = 4 and revises and relocates vote annotations. Minor spacing and pagination changes accompany the revision; empirical displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves internal consistency and reference traceability. Figure 1’s revised index p = 4 matches the displayed message 0001 under the paper’s one-based indexing, probability notation is standardized, and references provide fuller publication details. These are limited presentation improvements; the method, proof substance, and empirical validation are unchanged.
